links.note: Democracy against monarchy and dictatorship, answered by where power originates (the people vs a hereditary king vs one person's absolute hold) - 30779, the source-of-authority difference. 30780 is the mechanics of forming a government, which this answer touches only in passing.
Definition of democracy as rule by the people, directly or through chosen representatives - 30774.
Universal adult franchise is how the people exercise the authority 30775 says is theirs; 30774 is only the definition of the word democracy.
The odd one out is hereditary succession to government posts, which is 30780's contrast between forming a government by election and by family succession.
Accountability = the government answerable to the people, which follows directly from 30775's claim about where authority comes from.
Five-yearly Lok Sabha elections: the periodic election through which a democratic government is formed, 30780.
Ministers must resign on losing the confidence of the Lok Sabha - how a government is constituted and unmade in a democracy, 30780.
Aristocratic families ruling Greek city-states named as oligarchy: a form classified by who holds authority, which is 30779's axis.
Iran's mix of theocratic and democratic elements; theocracy is named inside 30779 as the contrast case to popular authority.
Executive drawn from and answerable to the legislature is the parliamentary way of forming a government - 30780.
The wrong pairing is King Charles III, who inherited rather than seized power; the item turns on monarchy versus dictatorship as ways a ruler comes to rule, 30780.
Statement item on dictatorship and the suppression of rights: a form classified by who holds authority, 30779. DEFECT: statements 1 and 2 are missing from the stored stem.
Chandrapida and the cobbler from the Rajatarangini is the chapter's illustration of a ruler bound by duty, which is 30769's opening frame (duty, not power).
The false Reason claims democracy is designed for a small elite; rejecting it requires 30774's definition of democracy as rule of the people, used as the test.
The Holocaust under Hitler appears in this chapter as what unchecked dictatorial authority produced; it belongs with the other dictatorship items on 30779.

'Adjudicating' is glossed where the chapter lists what a government does; settling disputes officially sits in 30772's law-and-order functions. (Items on judicial INDEPENDENCE as a safeguard are a different idea and I left those unlinked.)
Definition of a representative - 30777 is where representation is introduced, through the student committee, as the practical answer to who decides.
Swiss women enfranchised only in the 20th century: about who counts as 'the people' in whom authority rests, 30775.
Bhishma's Shanti Parva teaching on a raja's moral responsibilities is the classical statement of a ruler's duty, 30769.
What universal adult franchise guarantees - the people's exercise of authority, 30775.

Kautilya's Arthashastra appears here among the classical Indian texts on a ruler's duties and statecraft, which is 30769's 'classical formulation'. No Arthashastra concept exists in this chapter's set.
Characteristics of a dictatorship, i.e. authority held without the people's mandate - 30779.
'Rajadharma' as the duties expected of a king - 30769's duty frame.
'Rule of the people' is 30774 word for word.
Universal adult franchise named as the principle giving every adult a vote - 30775.
Switzerland 1971 recall, twin of the century MCQ - who is included in 'the people', 30775.
Direct democracy is rule of the people in its unmediated form, 30774; 30777 is reserved for items about why representation is used instead.
Accountability to the people who elected them - 30775.
'Vigilant citizens are the ultimate safeguard': the argument rests on the people being the source of authority, 30775.
Why direct democracy does not scale - exactly the problem 30777 answers by representation.
Parliamentary versus presidential executives: two ways a democratic government is formed and held, which 30780 covers ('other methods exist besides these two').
Limits on participation in ancient Greek republics qualifies what a republic is (an elected head of state, not necessarily a wide electorate) - 30781. 30782-83 are the Indian Lichchhavi case.
Rajadharma explained as duty binding the king - 30769.
Absolute versus constitutional monarchy: both are 30780's family-succession route, differing in how much power the crown keeps.
Theocracy's defining feature is that religious belief and religious leaders supply authority, which 30779 states outright.
Conditions in North Korea drawn from Shane's story - 30785. 30786 is narrower, the compulsory military service alone.
Oligarchy defined by who holds authority (a small elite) - 30779.
Why democracy is preferred to other forms: 30774's short definition is what the other forms are tested against, as its description says.
Direct versus representative democracy and why scale forces the latter - the representation concept, 30777.
Executive-legislature relation in the two democratic forms, i.e. how each government is constituted - 30780.
Rajadharma as a check on monarchical power - the duty-before-power frame of 30769.
Importance of universal adult franchise, answered as popular sovereignty - 30775.
